Fully mechanical verification, cost-adjusted. Pre-registered design: tools/arena/R5-DESIGN.md — written before any of these numbers existed. THIS FILE IS A REVIEWED PROMOTION of the harness receipt for run 2, with a review block and a full prior-run disclosure appended. No harness-emitted field was altered.
card: round-5-deep-reasoning: 6 tasks across 5 families where one wrong intermediate step propagates; fully mechanical verification; per-run token and cost accounting
harness: tools/arena/deep-reasoning.mjs — claude CLI print mode, default system prompt replaced
method: Each task is dispatched independently to every contestant with a minimal replaced system prompt and no tools. The reply's final ANSWER line is matched against pre-registered accepting regexes; a match against a pre-registered attractor is recorded as FAIL-ATTRACTOR. Binary scoring, no partial credit, no LLM judge.

summary.headline: REVIEWED VERDICT: VOID-EQUIVALENT. Mechanical spread is 1 task, but both non-PASS cells are non-reasoning (one transport error, one missing answer line); every tier answered correctly on every task it answered. Run 1 of the same card scored 6/6 across all four tiers outright. See review and priorRun. No routing change.
caveats: n=1 per (task, contestant) cell — directional, not statistical.
Zero LLM-judge dependence: every result is a regex match against a pre-registered ground truth.
model-in-Claude-Code-CLI, not raw API. The default system prompt is replaced to keep token accounting attributable, but this is still a harness measurement.
Cost is the CLI's own list-price attribution for the contestant's model entry; it excludes the background Haiku call the CLI makes per invocation.
inputTokens sums the uncached, cache-write and cache-read buckets. Reading only the uncached bucket under-reports a large prompt by orders of magnitude — see the harness comment in runClaude().
Effort is held constant across the three tiers that accept it and is not applied to claude-haiku-4-5, which does not support it. The cost-adjusted effort frontier is NOT measured by this round.
One round cannot harden a routing rule: the A2 floor requires >=2 concordant rounds.
At least one cell errored; treat any tier with errors > 0 as incompletely measured.

attestation: Built on SIP — Starlight Intelligence Protocol

priorRun.note: The card was executed TWICE on 2026-08-28. Both runs are disclosed here; neither is discarded. Run 1 is reported in full because publishing only run 2 would be selection.

run1.whySuperseded: Instrument defect in the token column only. The harness read the CLI usage field inputTokens, which excludes the cache-write and cache-read buckets, and therefore recorded values as low as 2 input tokens for an 18,500-token prompt. Run 1's PASS/FAIL data is unaffected and is reported below. The harness was corrected to sum all three buckets and the IDENTICAL card was re-run as run 2. The card itself was not changed between runs.
run1.outcome: Every contestant passed every task. Zero FAIL, zero FAIL-ATTRACTOR, zero NO-ANSWER, zero ERROR. Under the pre-registered void rule (R5-DESIGN.md section 4) a spread of 0 is VOID: a design failure, not a finding.

reasoning: The harness stamped run 2 verdict=MEASURED because the mechanical spread is 1 task. The reviewed reading is that this does not clear the pre-registered bar, for two independent reasons.
First, R5-DESIGN.md section 9 pre-registers that a spread of exactly 1 is weak separation and must NOT move the route at n=1.

Second, and decisive: NEITHER non-PASS cell is a reasoning failure. haiku/d2 is a transport ERROR (TLS: self-signed certificate detected at the sandbox proxy), which section 9 already rules unusable for a routing change. fable/d4 is NO-ANSWER: the model reasoned but did not emit the required final ANSWER line, which is an output-discipline failure and is the same signature R1, R2 and R3 all recorded on that axis. Remove both non-reasoning cells and every tier is at 100% on every task it answered.

Across both runs, 46 of 46 scored cells that produced an answer produced the CORRECT answer. Zero wrong answers. Not one of the twelve pre-registered attractors was taken by any tier — including claude-haiku-4-5 on the memorisation-inverting probability item and on the 300-section needle reconciliation.
review.headline: The card was built specifically to separate reasoning tiers and did not separate them. Capability is saturated across the entire lineup on well-posed, ground-truth-checkable reasoning tasks — the same result R3 reached on a far easier card, now reproduced against branch-flipping traps, a live decoy, a memorisation-inverting attractor, and a ten-constraint CSP.
review.routingConsequence: NONE. routing-table.json deep-reasoning stays route=opus, confidence=low, rounds=0, autoApply=false. A void-equivalent round does not count toward the A2 two-round floor. The class remains UNMEASURED in the sense that matters: the card never located an Opus or Fable ceiling, so the doctrine claim that Opus is the right tier for deep reasoning is still a hunch.
review.costObservationNotAFinding: With capability saturated, cost is the only axis that moved, and it moved against the expensive tiers. Cost per passed task in run 2: haiku $0.0157, sonnet $0.0101, opus $0.0207, fable $0.0360. In run 1: haiku $0.0239, sonnet $0.0279, opus $0.0698, fable $0.0665. Haiku reached the same answers using roughly 3-5x the output tokens of fable and was still cheaper. This is consistent with the doctrine rule that a saturated class routes to the cheapest passing tier, but it is NOT evidence for a routing change: a saturated card cannot tell you what the expensive tiers are for. Do not cite these numbers as a finding.
whatWouldActuallySeparate: The tiers are no longer separated by whether they can solve well-posed deterministic problems. That capability is now common to the whole lineup, Haiku included.

This creates a methodological bind for R6: the tasks that plausibly still separate the frontier — open-ended synthesis, long-horizon multi-step agentic work, judgment under genuine ambiguity — are exactly the tasks with no mechanical ground truth, and R5 could not use a judge because all four tiers were contestants.

AMENDED 2026-09-19 (round renumbered R4 -> R5; arena R4 is the 2026-06-10 work-samples card, which this mirror never received). The original text here read: 'R6 therefore needs the cross-family judge from ROUTING-DOCTRINE.md roadmap item 2 before a harder card is worth building.' That is wrong. Arena R4 already ran two blind Claude-family sonnet judges with shuffled per-task labels over real production work and recorded family bias as a stated caveat, not a blocker. R6 is NOT gated on the cross-family judge existing; that judge reduces a known bias rather than unlocking the method. Building a harder mechanical card first is still likely to saturate again.

AMENDED 2026-09-19: arena R4 also separated the tiers on an axis this card does not measure — discipline under load. Its recorded finding: 'Fable 5 violated an output contract for the first time across four rounds — when the task itself is heavy, its constraint edge narrows', with Opus at 5 of 7 structured-output tasks violated. This receipt classifies run 2 fable/d4 (correct chain, omitted ANSWER line, the heaviest multi-file task on the card) as non-reasoning and therefore noise. Against R4 it is not noise: it is a third independent instance of the same measured behaviour from the tier R4 named. The reasoning verdict is unchanged — no tier gave a wrong answer — but that cell is evidence on the output-discipline axis, not an absence of evidence.

AMENDED 2026-09-19: second cheap probe, alongside the effort sweep — re-score the replies this round already produced for OUTPUT-CONTRACT COMPLIANCE rather than correctness. Mechanical, no judge, no new spend, and it tests the one axis four rounds now agree on.

Cheaper interim probe: hold this card fixed and sweep effort DOWNWARD. If every tier still passes at effort=low, the routing question stops being which tier and becomes which effort — and that saving is larger than any tier swap.
